title: Arrow functions
learningObjectives: Explain arrow functions and use functions with clear scope and behaviour.

understand.concept: Arrow functions provide a concise function expression syntax using =>. They have lexical this, do not have their own arguments object, and cannot be used as constructors. They are often useful for callbacks and short functions.
understand.whyItMatters: Arrow functions are not simply shorter function declarations; their this behaviour differs from ordinary functions. Choose the syntax based on the intended behaviour and readability.
understand.analogy: An arrow function is a compact way to describe a function, but it follows different rules for its surrounding this value.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; function execution, scope, closures, and call stacks follow JavaScript runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The first arrow function has one parameter and an expression body. The second uses two parameters and returns their sum.

examples.explanation: The first arrow function has one parameter and an expression body. The second uses two parameters and returns their sum.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function results described.

practise.guidedTask: Rewrite a function expression as an arrow function. Compare an arrow callback with a regular function when this is involved.
practise.independentTask: Build a small reusable function example. Test inputs, scope boundaries, and any retained state or side effects.
hints: Keep functions focused and names descriptive.
Know whether a callback is synchronous or asynchronous.
Add a base case to every recursive function.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Arrow functions</title></head><body>
<script>const double=value=>value*2;const add=(left,right)=>left+right;console.log(double(4),add(3,5));</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What is a key difference between arrow functions and ordinary functions?
options: Arrow functions use lexical this and do not have their own this
questions.answer: Arrow functions use lexical this and do not have their own this
questions.explanation: Arrow functions capture this from their surrounding lexical scope.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reason about?
options: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.answer: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.explanation: Explicit dependencies and controlled side effects improve clarity and testability.
